what_is_closed: M9-B: the 16-cell (T, G_c) design surface. The grid is complete, the claims are fixed at the width the evidence supports, and the artifacts are hashed. Reopening it means a new freeze, not an edit.
claim: In the investigated grid, increasing test duration systematically raised r_EVSI for the tools that had an informative VERDICT at all, while increasing the donor pool from 5 to 40 showed no comparable stable gain. The donor result is 'no convincing evidence of appreciable benefit over this range', NOT a demonstrated null.

inference_status.reportable: paired contrasts with the OTHER axis held fixed, and their 95% credible intervals
inference_status.excluded_from_axis_claims: the T15_G05 -> T42_G40 span, which moves both axes and characterises a change of design rather than either axis

duration_T15_to_T42_at_fixed_G.note: 8 of 12 among tools with an informative verdict; geolift 0/4 flat

compute.units_warning: three DIFFERENT quantities. Pass 2's 40.3 process-hours occupied ~13 h of clock on an oversubscribed 4-core box, so none is a CPU-hour in the sense the estimate used and none is comparable to another.
compute.attributable_to_F21: pass 2 was NECESSITATED by F21 (a PATH bug meant the two R tools never executed on pass 1). Not all of its 40.3 process-hours were avoidable: the R-tool estimation was always required, and run_tools runs the three estimators in one thread pool, so on a correct first pass it would have been partly masked by CausalPy's MCMC. Measured per-panel: pass 1 13.8 s, pass 2 22.7 s. The avoidable portion is the unmasked remainder plus re-orchestration and is not separable from the executed figures.

not_established: that any of this transports outside a synthetic DGP containing no spend, no budget and no intervention
that donor pool size is irrelevant to geo experiments
that the monotonicity direction counts would survive a preregistered test
that M9-B cells are comparable to the donor's A1/A3 -- 21 geos drawn as 41 and sliced is a different world from 21 drawn as 21

amendments.kind: factual correction to the write-up, plus one defect in the closure record itself; NO data, claim or artifact changed
amendments.what: The compute section said 'the whole of pass 2 is attributable to F21 and was avoidable'. The second half is false. run_tools.py submits causalpy, geolift and causalimpact to one ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3), so on a correct first pass the R tools would have run CONCURRENTLY with CausalPy's MCMC. The 40.3 process-hours of R-tool estimation were always required by the design; F21 cost the portion concurrency would have masked plus re-orchestration, which cannot be cleanly separated from the executed figures. Corrected to 'pass 2 was necessitated by F21'.
amendments.why_not_a_reopening: no cell, seed, estimate, claim or interval moved. The experiment is untouched; a sentence about accounting was wrong. Recorded as an amendment rather than edited silently, because a closure record that can be quietly rewritten is not a closure record.
also: named the C12 pattern a PROXY-PRESERVING ADVERSARIAL WITNESS and related it to the test-oracle problem: the failure mode is choosing a surrogate relation the defect also satisfies, which a generic negative fixture cannot expose
recorded the three mechanism questions M9-B narrows to

CAUGHT BY THIS RE-HASH: docs/m9-preregistration.md was already stale in the committed closure record. The record was generated, and the 'M9-B - CLOSED' section was appended to the preregistration afterwards in the same turn, so the hash shipped describing a file that no longer existed in that form. A closure record whose own hashes are taken before the last write is a closure record that certifies nothing. The generator should hash as its final act, or refuse on a dirty tree -- noted here rather than fixed silently, and it is the same presence-vs-substance family as F22: I checked that hashes were RECORDED, not that they were CURRENT.

narrows_to.note: M9-B's value is that the next experiment is a mechanism question, not a wider grid. None of these is scheduled.
questions: DURATION — by what mechanism does additional time reach decision value, and where does it saturate? The grid stops at 42 post-days and the duration gradient has not flattened inside it.

DECISION INTERFACE / SIGN LOSS — how much information is destroyed specifically by the transform estimator output -> VERDICT, as opposed to by the estimator? V-B rises with design richness by point estimate and has not had the paired-interval treatment.
GEOLIFT — why does a far richer design barely move r_EVSI(VERDICT)? Three candidates, not separated here: an estimator limitation, a verdict-representation artefact, or a property of this DGP.
narrows_to.deprioritised: a wider donor pool. Not because donors are shown irrelevant -- see not_established -- but because 5 -> 40 has been paid for once and returned a weak signal.
